title: Fecal microbiota transplantation accelerates clearance of carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales intestinal carriage: influence of recipient gut microbiome ecology.
abstract: Background Persistent intestinal carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales (CPE) carriage challenges infection prevention and antimicrobial stewardship. We evaluated fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) for decolonization and response-associated recipient microbiome features. Methods This prospective cohort study assessed intestinal CPE clearance in 131 adult carriers (68 receiving FMT; 63 under observation). Responders achieved clearance, defined as three consecutive negative rectal surveillance cultures for CPE, obtained at 3-day intervals within 1 month after FMT. Following least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO)-based covariate selection, Cox proportional hazards models estimated associations between FMT and time to successful decolonization within prespecified 0-30-day and 0-90-day windows. A longitudinal metagenomic subcohort of 21 FMT recipients (102 fecal samples) underwent shotgun sequencing to characterize taxonomic composition, microbial network organization, functional pathways, antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs), and donor engraftment. Results After LASSO-based covariate selection, FMT was associated with faster CPE clearance than observation at 1 month (hazard ratio, 4.02; 95% confidence interval, 1.84-8.79), with effects sustained at 3 months. Responders showed relatively preserved baseline microbial network organization and enrichment of taxa annotated with arginine-related pathway features, suggesting metabolic relevance to microbial niche competition. After FMT, responders had greater engraftment of donor-associated taxa and donor-like ecological reassembly, with reduced Klebsiella pneumoniae dominance and ARG abundance. Conclusions FMT may accelerate intestinal decolonization in CPE carriers; response variability was associated with recipient gut-microbiome ecology, suggesting microbiome-guided patient selection could optimize microbiota-based strategies.
authors: Lee I, Suk KT, Park JY, Yong D, Kim DJ, Kim BS, Lee SS.
screening_reason: Focuses on fecal microbiota transplantation and recipient gut microbiome ecology during intestinal CPE decolonization.
summary_ja: カルバペネマーゼ産生腸内細菌目細菌（CPE）の腸内保有者131名を対象に、糞便微生物移植（FMT）による脱定着効果を検討した前瞻的コホート研究である。FMT群は観察群と比較して1か月および3か月時点でのCPEクリアランスが有意に促進された。ショットガンメタゲノム解析の結果、治療反応者ではベースライン時の細菌ネットワーク構造が維持されており、アルギニン関連代謝経路の富集が見られた。FMT後、反応者ではドナー由来の菌の生着と生態系再構築が進行し、薬剤耐性遺伝子の存在量が減少した。
summary_en: A prospective cohort study evaluated the efficacy of fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) for clearing intestinal carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales carriage in adults. FMT significantly accelerated CPE clearance compared with observation over 1-month and 3-month follow-up windows. Metagenomic analysis revealed that clinical response was associated with recipient baseline gut microbiome ecology and enhanced donor strain engraftment.
key_finding_ja: FMTはCPE腸内保有者の除菌を加速させ、その治療反応性は受容者のベースライン時の腸内細菌叢生態系と関連していた。
why_it_matters_ja: 腸内細菌叢の生態学的特徴に基づく患者選定が、多剤耐性菌の脱定着を目的としたマイクロバイオーム療法の最適化に役立つ可能性がある。

title: Immunopharmacological mechanisms underlying SARS-CoV-2 spike-induced persistent pain in mice.
abstract: SARS-CoV-2 infection is frequently associated with persistent pain, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Given that viral structural proteins can act as pathogen-associated molecular patterns, we investigated whether the Spike protein is sufficient to induce long-lasting nociceptive alterations and the immune pathways involved. Intraplantar administration of recombinant Spike protein in mice elicited robust and persistent mechanical and thermal hypersensitivity, accompanied by transient local inflammation, sustained systemic cytokine alterations, and prolonged spinal neuroinflammation. Spike-induced paw inflammation and persistent mechanical hypersensitivity were dependent on Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4), as both pharmacological inhibition and genetic deficiency of TLR4 abolished these responses. Mechanistically, depletion of mononuclear phagocytes or blockade of T-cell co-stimulation prevented the development of persistent mechanical hypersensitivity, supporting a role for coordinated innate and adaptive immune mechanisms in the establishment of long-lasting nociceptive sensitization. In parallel, Spike induced increases in lymphocyte-associated cytokines, including IFN-γ, IL-4, and IL-17, with modest and transient changes in peripheral compartments but pronounced and sustained elevations in the spinal cord. Among these, IFN-γ emerged as a critical contributor to these responses, as its genetic deletion abolished both inflammation and persistent hypersensitivity. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that the SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein is sufficient to trigger persistent pain-like states through a TLR4-driven neuroimmune cascade involving phagocytes, T cells, and IFN-γ signaling. This study provides mechanistic insight into neuroimmune pathways that may contribute to persistent pain following SARS-CoV-2 infection and establishes a tractable mechanistic experimental model for investigating Spike-induced neuroimmune mechanisms of chronic pain.
authors: de Lima Almeida B, Pereira S, Primicheru LI, Vitorino LC, Goldoni FC, Fernandes OKF, Rasga GL, da Cruz Nunes M, Manjavachi MN, D'Oliveira GSM, Freixo PF, de Matos Guedes HL, Figueiredo CP, Quintão NLM, Bevan S, Passos GF, da Costa R.
screening_reason: Mechanistic study demonstrating that SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein induces chronic pain via a TLR4-dependent neuroimmune cascade and spinal neuroinflammation.
summary_ja: SARS-CoV-2のスパイクタンパク質がマウスにおいて持続的な痛覚過敏を引き起こす免疫薬理学的メカニズムを解明した研究である。足底へのスパイクタンパク質投与は、局所炎症だけでなく持続的な脊髄の神経炎症と機械的・熱的痛覚過敏を誘発した。この病態はTLR4依存的であり、単核食細胞の除去やT細胞共刺激の阻害、あるいはIFN-γの遺伝子欠損により過敏状態が消失した。したがって、スパイクタンパク質は食細胞やT細胞、IFN-γシグナルが関与するTLR4駆動型神経免疫カスケードを介して持続痛を引き起こす。
summary_en: Intraplantar administration of SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein in mice induced persistent pain-like hypersensitivity and sustained spinal neuroinflammation. This response was mediated by TLR4 and required mononuclear phagocytes, T-cell co-stimulation, and IFN-γ signaling. The study demonstrates that Spike protein alone is sufficient to trigger long-lasting pain via a specific neuroimmune axis.
key_finding_ja: SARS-CoV-2のスパイクタンパク質は、TLR4、食細胞、T細胞、およびIFN-γが関与する神経免疫カスケードを介して持続的な痛覚過敏を誘導する。
why_it_matters_ja: SARS-CoV-2感染後に生じる持続性疼痛のメカニズム解明や、神経免疫経路を標的とした治療法開発に寄与する可能性がある。

title: Dysbiosis of the oral-gut microbiome axis in a mouse model of depression.
abstract: This study aimed to characterize the alterations in both oral and gut microbiota in a mouse model of depression and to explore their potential role in the pathogenesis of major depressive disorder (MDD) through the oral-gut-brain axis. A depression model was established in male C57BL/6J mice using chronic social defeat stress (CSDS) paradigm. Depressive phenotypes were confirmed through social interaction, sucrose preference, open field, tail suspension, and forced swim tests. The microbial composition of oral and gut samples was analyzed using 16S rRNA sequencing, with Linear Discriminant Analysis Effect Size (LEfSe) employed to identify differentially abundant taxa and Spearman correlation analysis to examine microbiota-behavior relationships. CSDS successfully induced robust depression-like behaviors, including social avoidance, anhedonia, and behavioral despair. Beta-diversity analysis revealed significant separation in oral microbiota between CSDS and control groups. LEfSe analysis identified distinct microbial signatures: control mice were enriched in oral Streptococcus and gut commensals including Lachnospiraceae, Bacteroides and Oscillospiraceae, whereas CSDS mice showed expansion of oral Muribacter and Rodentibacter and gut Alloprevotella, Helicobacter and Colidextribacter. Correlation analyses demonstrated significant associations between specific microbial patterns and depression-like behaviors, with control-enriched taxa negatively correlating with behavioral deficits. Furthermore, significant cross-habitat microbial correlations were observed between oral and gut differential taxa. Our findings demonstrate that CSDS induces divergent microbial alterations in both oral and gut ecosystems, which are systematically associated with depression-like behaviors. These results provide compelling evidence for the involvement of the oral-gut-brain axis in depression pathophysiology and suggest that modulating these microbial ecosystems may represent a potential therapeutic strategy for MDD.
authors: Lei P, Tong S, Xi W, Liu Y, Yu J, Yu L, Zhao B, Jia M, Li Y, Ma X, Wang Y, Guo Y.
screening_reason: Directly investigates oral and gut microbiome alterations and their association with depression-like behaviors in a mouse model.
summary_ja: 慢性的社会的挫折ストレス（CSDS）によるうつ病マウスモデルを用いて、口腔および腸内細菌叢の変化を解析した。16S rRNAメタゲノム解析により、対照群とうつ病モデル群で口腔および腸内の細菌組成が大きく異なることが示された。対照群では口腔 Streptococcus や腸内 Lachnospiraceae などが豊富であったのに対し、CSDS群では口腔 Muribacter や腸内 Alloprevotella などが増加していた。特定細菌の存在比はうつ様行動と相関し、口腔と腸の細菌間にも相互関連が認められた。
summary_en: Using a chronic social defeat stress mouse model of depression, this study evaluated alterations in oral and gut microbiota via 16S rRNA sequencing. CSDS mice exhibited distinct microbial signatures compared to controls, including the expansion of specific oral and gut taxa. These microbial patterns significantly correlated with depression-like behaviors and revealed cross-habitat correlations between oral and gut communities.
key_finding_ja: 慢性的社会的挫折ストレスを与えたマウスでは、口腔および腸内の細菌叢に特徴的な構成変化が生じ、それらがうつ様行動と有意に相関していた。
why_it_matters_ja: 口腔・腸・脳軸を介したマイクロバイオームの変動が抑うつ病態に関与する可能性を示しており、細菌叢の調節が新たな治療戦略につながるかもしれない。

title: Bile acids as mediators of microbiota signaling in entero-hepatic disorders.
abstract: This review examines the structure and the functional role of the signaling network formed by bile acids as their receptors in mediating chemical communication between the intestinal microbiota and host in entero-hepatic disorders, such as inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD). In the last decade, advances in analytical technologies and bioinformatic approaches, including metabolomics and reverse metabolomics, have greatly expanded our understanding of bile acid metabolism. These studies have shown that the intestinal microbiota transforms primary bile acids synthesized in the liver from cholesterol into a highly diverse family of bioactive mediators. Hundred of "classical" secondary bile acids and Microbial Derived Bile Acids (MDBA) have been identified and characterized for their role in regulating the activity of widely expressed receptors, including the Farnesoid-x-receptor (FXR), the G protein-coupled bile acid receptor (GPBAR1) and the retinoid-related orphan receptor (RORγ). Simultaneous characterization of microbial species expressing bile acid-related genes is emerging as a valuable tool for disease phenotyping. One example is bile salt hydrolase (BSH), an enzyme that catalyzes bile acid deconjugation. In parallel, profiling bile acid composition in biological compartments such as feces and blood may help identify associations between microbiota dysbiosis and diseases including IBD and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). The review also examines therapeutic approaches that could be developed to exploit this novel conceptual framework.
authors: Fiorucci S, Marchianò S, Giorgio CD, Urbani G, Monti MC, Zampella A, Distrutti E, Biagioli M.
screening_reason: The paper examines host-microbe interactions, intestinal microbial metabolism of bile acids, and host receptor signaling in entero-hepatic disorders.
summary_ja: 本レビューは、炎症性腸疾患（IBD）や代謝異常関連脂肪肝疾患（MASLD）などの腸肝疾患における、腸内細菌叢と宿主間のシグナル伝達物質としての胆汁酸の役割を解説している。メタボロミクス技術の進展により、腸内細菌が一次胆汁酸を多様な生物活性を持つ二次胆汁酸や微生物由来胆汁酸へ変換することが明示された。これらの胆汁酸はFXRやGPBAR1、RORγなどの受容体を介して機能し、胆汁酸塩水解酵素（BSH）などの酵素遺伝子を保有する菌種の同定が病態分類に利用されている。著者らは糞便や血液中の胆汁酸プロファイル解析と概念的枠組みに基づく治療法開発の可能性を論じている。
summary_en: This review discusses bile acids as key molecular signaling links between the gut microbiota and the host in entero-hepatic disorders, such as inflammatory bowel disease and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. Advanced metabolomic approaches have revealed that gut bacteria convert liver-derived primary bile acids into a diverse pool of bioactive secondary bile acids and microbial-derived bile acids that target receptors like FXR and GPBAR1. The authors highlight the potential of profiling microbial bile acid-metabolizing pathways for disease phenotyping and novel therapeutic target discovery.
key_finding_ja: 腸内細菌が生成する多種多様な二次胆汁酸および微生物由来胆汁酸が、宿主の胆汁酸受容体を介して腸肝疾患の病態調節を担うシグナル因子であることが概括された。
why_it_matters_ja: 胆汁酸代謝を中心とした腸内細菌叢と宿主の相互作用の解明は、炎症性腸疾患や代謝性肝疾患の精密な病態診断や新たな治療法開発につながる可能性がある。

title: Astrocyte-Microglia Crosstalk in Post-Hemorrhagic Neurovascular Microenvironment: Mechanistic Nodes, Cross-Stroke Comparisons, and Therapeutic Reprogramming.
abstract: Background Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) produces a rapidly evolving and spatially heterogeneous neurovascular microenvironment in which secondary injury is shaped not only by hematoma volume and location, but also by the interaction of blood-derived toxins, blood-brain barrier disruption, edema, oxidative stress, protease activity, and glial responses. Increasing evidence suggests that these processes are better understood as dynamic network events rather than isolated inflammatory pathways. Main body This review applies a network-centered framework to astrocyte-microglia coupling, viewing it as a critical control layer that may either support injury containment and hematoma resolution or drive persistent neurotoxicity and failed repair. Comparisons with ischemic stroke are used to distinguish shared inflammatory modules from hemorrhage-specific drivers, including heme, hemoglobin, iron overload, thrombin, fibrinogen, and clot-associated protease signaling. Integrating findings from single-cell and spatially resolved studies, the review summarizes the temporal and spatial organization of post-hemorrhagic microenvironment remodeling and discusses astrocyte-dependent regulation of barrier function, edema dynamics, immunometabolism, redox buffering, and synaptic homeostasis. It also examines how astrocyte-derived cues influence microglial state transitions through danger sensing, inflammasome signaling, cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon (IFN) genes signaling, phagocytic containment, iron-handling programs, complement-mediated synaptic vulnerability, and interaction with infiltrating myeloid cells. Recurring astrocyte-microglia network motifs are further evaluated as therapeutic control points, with emphasis on how lesion stage and spatial compartmentalization shape intervention windows for purinergic, chemokine, cytokine, IFN, complement-coagulation, and lipid/iron signaling pathways. Translational priorities, limitations, and therapeutic opportunities are discussed across hematoma-toxicity reduction, barrier and edema repair, network reprogramming, and regenerative microenvironment shaping. Conclusion Meaningful improvement in ICH outcome will likely depend on biomarker-guided and stage-specific reprogramming of astrocyte-microglia network dynamics to restore microenvironmental balance, rather than on nonspecific suppression of neuroinflammation.
authors: Ye F, Chen R, Xu S, Liu H, Xu J.
screening_reason: The review focuses centrally on astrocyte-microglia crosstalk, neuroinflammatory cascades, and microglial state transitions following intracerebral hemorrhage.
summary_ja: 本レビュー論文は、脳内出血後の微小環境におけるアストロサイトとミクログリアの相互作用とその役割を網羅的に解説している。著者らは、出血後に生じる複雑な病態現象を単一の炎症経路ではなく、動的なネットワーク応答として捉える重要性を提示した。血腫由来毒素やヘム、鉄過剰などの出血特異的因子と虚血性脳卒中の共通因子を比較し、ミクログリアのフェノタイプ変化やアストロサイトのバリア調節機構をまとめている。また、病期や局所特異性に応じた制御ポイントを同定し、神経炎症の制御に向けた治療戦略を論じた。
summary_en: This review outlines the dynamic network interactions between astrocytes and microglia within the neurovascular microenvironment following intracerebral hemorrhage. By comparing hemorrhagic pathways with ischemic stroke modules, the authors highlight how hemorrhage-specific factors like heme and iron overload shape glial responses and microenvironmental remodeling. The article emphasizes that stage- and region-specific therapeutic reprogramming of astrocyte-microglia networks represents a more effective strategy than non-specific neuroinflammation suppression.
key_finding_ja: 脳内出血後のアストロサイトとミクログリアの網羅的ネットワーク解析に基づき、病期に応じた相互作用の再プログラミングが新たな治療アプローチとして提案された。
why_it_matters_ja: 脳内出血の二次的損傷を抑制するためには、単なる微小炎症の抑制ではなく病期や空間的特性に応じた細やかな神経免疫ネットワークの制御が重要であることが示唆される。

title: Antibiotic Mixture Exposure in Meconium Affects Child Neurodevelopment via Altering Early-Life Gut Microbiome and Metabolome.
abstract: Previous evidence has established associations of antibiotic exposure in early life with neurodevelopmental disorders. However, previous studies have often relied on self-reported or record-based exposure measures that may not accurately reflect internal fetal exposure, and few have integrated prenatal exposure biomarkers with infant microbiome, metabolome, and longitudinal neurodevelopmental data. This study included 300 mother-infant pairs from the Shanghai Maternal-Child Pairs Cohort. Meconium samples were used to quantify concentrations of 18 antibiotics using high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC). Neurodevelopmental outcomes were assessed using Ages and Stages Questionnaires (ASQ) at 2, 6, 12, and 24 months of age. Multi-omics profiling of 6-month fecal samples was conducted, employing 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing and HPLC-based metabolomics. Linear and logistic regression models, negative binomial regression, interpretable machine learning algorithms, metabolome-wide association/pathway analyses and high-dimensional mediation modeling were used. Our study population demonstrated predominant exposure to three antibiotics: chlortetracycline, penicillin, and chloramphenicol. Each interquartile range (IQR) increase in meconium-measured antibiotic burden was associated with a lower total ASQ score at 6 months (β = -4.49, 95% CI: -7.14 to -1.86) and lower scores across all five developmental domains (βs ranging from -0.53 to -1.11; all P < 0.05). Each IQR increment of antibiotic burden was also associated with greater odds of belonging to the lower-score group of total ASQ trajectory (OR = 1.20, 95% CI: 1.04, 1.42) and the lower-score group of personal-social trajectory (OR = 1.13, 95% CI: 1.01, 1.28). Exploratory high-dimensional mediation analyses identified Lactobacillus and 2-(14,15-epoxyeicosatrienoyl) glycerol (2-14,15-EG) as candidate intermediates in the association between meconium-measured antibiotic burden and neurodevelopment. Our study suggested that higher meconium-based biomarkers of intrauterine antibiotic burden were significantly associated with lower neurodevelopmental outcomes in early childhood, with the strongest inverse associations observed at 6 months. Lactobacillus and 2-14,15-EG were identified as potential mediator biomarkers. These hypothesis-generating findings require independent replication, longitudinal temporal validation, and experimental studies before causal mechanisms or microbiota-targeted interventions can be inferred.
authors: Zhou Y, Wang F, Zhao Y, Wang H, Ma W, Shi H, Zhang Y.
screening_reason: The study investigates how intrauterine antibiotic exposure affects child neurodevelopment through changes in early-life gut microbiome composition and microbial metabolomics.
summary_ja: 母子コホート300組を対象に、胎便中の18種類の抗菌薬濃度測定と生後6か月時の腸内細菌叢・代謝物メタボローム解析を行い、24か月までの神経発達との関連を調べた。胎便中の抗菌薬暴露量が多いほど、生後6か月時点のASQスコア低下および低い発達トラジェクトリーに属するリスクの上昇が観察された。高次元媒介解析により、Lactobacillus属と代謝物2-14,15-EGが抗菌薬暴露と神経発達低下を結ぶ潜在的な仲介因子として特定された。胎児期の抗菌薬暴露が乳幼児の神経発達に悪影響を与える可能性が示唆された。
summary_en: In a prospective cohort of 300 mother-infant pairs, meconium antibiotic levels were quantified alongside infant gut microbiome and metabolome profiles at 6 months to assess child neurodevelopment through 24 months. Higher internal fetal antibiotic exposure correlated with lower neurodevelopmental scores and persistently poorer developmental trajectories. Mediation analyses indicated that infant Lactobacillus levels and the metabolite 2-14,15-EG candidate-mediated these neurodevelopmental impacts.
key_finding_ja: 胎児期の抗菌薬暴露負荷は乳幼児の神経発達低下と関連し、乳児期の腸内細菌Lactobacillusと代謝物2-14,15-EGがその媒介候補として同定された。
why_it_matters_ja: 周産期抗菌薬使用のリスク評価や腸内細菌叢を介した予防介入法の開発に役立つ可能性があるが、因果関係の解明にはさらなる実証研究が必要である。

title: Gut microbiome: a key driver and therapeutic target of intestinal fibrosis in Crohn's disease.
abstract: Intestinal fibrosis is a debilitating complication of Crohn's disease that often leads to stricture formation, requiring surgical intervention. Despite its clinical significance, effective anti-fibrotic therapies remain an unmet need. Emerging evidence highlights the gut microbiome as a central orchestrator of fibrogenesis, beyond its role in inflammation. This review provides a comprehensive overview of how microbial dysbiosis, which is marked by the expansion of pathobionts such as adherent-invasive Escherichia coli and Clostridium innocuum, drives intestinal fibrosis through multifaceted pathways. We delineate the direct activation of fibroblasts via pattern recognition receptors and indirect mechanisms involving macrophage polarization, T helper 17 cell responses, and the emerging role of the "creeping fat" axis. Furthermore, we discuss how microbial translocation into the mesenteric adipose tissue triggers a profibrotic environment. By synthesizing these mechanistic insights, we suggest that targeting the microbiome-fibrosis axis, through precision modulation of the microbiome or metabolite-based interventions, represents a promising frontier for preventing and reversing fibrostenotic Crohn's disease.
authors: Kim JH, Choi YJ, Yoo JH.
screening_reason: Comprehensive mechanistic review detailing how gut microbial dysbiosis drives intestinal fibrosis in Crohn's disease.
summary_ja: クローン病における合併症である腸管線維化と腸内細菌叢との関連をまとめたレビュー論文である。付着侵襲性大腸菌や Clostridium innocuum などの病原体様細菌の増加が、線維芽細胞の直接活性化や免疫細胞・脂肪組織を介して線維化を進行させることが解説されている。腸間膜脂肪組織への細菌転移が線維化促進環境を形成するメカニズムも議論されている。マイクロバイオームや代謝物を標的とした精密な介入が、線維化の予防・逆転における新たな治療法となる可能性を提示している。
summary_en: This review summarizes the role of the gut microbiome as a driver and therapeutic target of intestinal fibrosis in Crohn's disease. Pathobionts like AIEC and Clostridium innocuum promote fibrogenesis through direct fibroblast activation and indirect neuroimmune/inflammatory responses. Precision targeting of the microbiome-fibrosis axis represents a promising therapeutic approach for fibrostenotic Crohn's disease.
key_finding_ja: クローン病における腸管線維化は、特定の病原体様細菌が線維芽細胞や脂肪組織・免疫系を介して引き起こす複合的な機序によって推進される。
why_it_matters_ja: 細菌叢やその代謝物を標的とする新しい精密治療法が、難治性であるクローン病の狭窄・線維化の克服に寄与する可能性がある。

title: Global gut microbiome atlas identifies epidemiologic-stage-specific signatures in inflammatory bowel disease.
abstract: The global rise of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) reflects environmental shifts, yet how these changes are embedded in the gut microbial ecology remains unclear. We construct a microbiome atlas comprising 245,627 profiles. By classifying countries into three epidemiologic stages, we establish a framework. As the IBD burden increases, the gut microbial alpha diversity declines, and community structures form distinct clusters. This transition is characterized by a gradient of core genera. Integrating six shotgun metagenomic cohorts, we identify the depletion of anabolic pathways in IBD patients. Strain-level analysis reveals that epidemiologic staging shapes genetic architecture within species, identifying an IBD-enriched subclade of Eisenbergiella associated with elevated fecal cholic acid. We develop a microbial inflammatory risk score (MIRS), based on 19 genera, that discriminates IBD from controls (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.92). MIRS correlates with IBD prevalence. Our study provides an atlas linking epidemiology to microbiome ecology and strain evolution, offering a foundation for population-level surveillance and interventions in IBD.
authors: Zhai J, Li Y, Liu J, Su X, Cui R, Zheng D, Sun Y, Yu J, Dai C.
screening_reason: Constructs a global gut microbiome atlas to identify stage-specific gut microbial signatures and functional pathways in inflammatory bowel disease.
summary_ja: 24万サンプル以上のマイクロバイオームデータから、炎症性腸疾患（IBD）の疫学段階に応じた世界的な腸内細菌叢アトラスを構築した。IBDの疾患負担が大きい地域ほど、腸内細菌叢のα多様性が低下し、特異な群集構造を示すことが明らかになった。メタゲノム解析によりIBD患者での同化経路の欠損や、コール酸上昇に関連する Eisenbergiella の特定のサブクレードが特定された。さらに、19の属に基づく細菌性炎症リスクスコア（MIRS）を開発し、高い精度でIBDを識別できることを示した。
summary_en: A global gut microbiome atlas of 245,627 profiles was constructed to identify signatures across epidemiologic stages of inflammatory bowel disease. Higher IBD disease burden correlated with decreased alpha diversity and specific genus-level shift patterns. The study identified IBD-associated metabolic shifts, strain-level evolution in Eisenbergiella, and established a 19-genus risk score that effectively discriminates IBD.
key_finding_ja: IBDの地域的疫学段階に対応した腸内細菌叢アトラスを構築し、高い精度でIBDを識別する19属ベースの微生物リスクスコアを開発した。
why_it_matters_ja: 集団レベルでのIBDの監視や生態学的知見に基づいた介入手法の基盤となる可能性がある。

title: Does high fructose consumption trigger microglia activation and neuroinflammation? A systematic review.
abstract: This systematic review evaluated the effects of fructose intake on neuroinflammatory markers in rodent models. The search terms Fructose AND neuroinflammation OR Neurodegeneration OR chemokines OR interleukins OR microglia OR behaviour OR memory OR cognition were used in Google Scholar, Scopus and Web of Science. Thirteen animal studies investigating fructose-induced neuroinflammation that matched the eligibility criteria were included in the study. Across the studies, 16 inflammatory markers were identified as significantly altered following exposure to fructose. The findings consistently demonstrated elevated expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines, TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β, following fructose administration. Fructose consumption also dysregulated MCP-1, fractalkine, and CX3CR1 levels, thereby promoting inflammatory signalling and microglial activation. Furthermore, fructose exposure significantly increased IBA-1 and CD11b, indicating sustained neuroimmune activation. Alterations in important inflammatory pathways involving TLR4, NLRP3, NF-κB, MyD88, iNOS, and cyclooxygenases (COX-1 and COX-2) were also observed. In contrast, expression of the anti-inflammatory regulator peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPARγ) was reduced after fructose treatment. Overall, the findings suggest that chronic fructose consumption induces neuroinflammation through multiple inflammatory and immune-related mechanisms in the brain. These effects appear to be dose- and duration-dependent and may contribute significantly to neurodegeneration and cognitive impairment.
authors: Olasehinde TA, Hernandez-Ledesma B, Cortes-Gomez P, Olaokun O, Olaniran AO.
journal: Food and chemical toxicology : an international journal published for the British Industrial Biological Research Association
screening_reason: The systematic review evaluates microglial activation, pro-inflammatory signaling pathways, and neuroinflammation induced by high fructose consumption.
summary_ja: 本系統的レビューは、果糖（フルクトース）の過剰摂取が齧歯類モデルの脳内神経炎症に与える影響を調査した13件の動物実験論文を評価した。解析の結果、果糖投与によりTNF-α、IL-6、IL-1βなどの前炎性サイトカインの上昇が共通して確認された。さらに、IBA-1やCD11bの発現増加によるミクログリアの持続的活性化や、TLR4、NLRP3、NF-κB経路の異常活性化が観察された。一方で抗炎症に関与するPPARγの発現低下も確認され、果糖の持続的摂取が用量および期間依存的に脳内神経炎症を引き起こすことが示された。
summary_en: This systematic review evaluated 13 animal studies examining the impact of chronic fructose intake on neuroinflammatory responses in rodent models. The findings consistently demonstrated that fructose consumption elevated pro-inflammatory cytokines, activated microglial markers such as IBA-1 and CD11b, and dysregulated signaling pathways including TLR4, NLRP3, and NF-κB. These results suggest that high fructose intake induces dose- and duration-dependent neuroinflammation, which may contribute to neurodegeneration and cognitive decline.
key_finding_ja: 齧歯類モデルに関する系統的レビューにより、高果糖摂取が前炎性サイトカインの増加およびミクログリアの活性化を介して脳内神経炎症を誘発することが確認された。
why_it_matters_ja: 食習慣による果糖の過剰摂取が脳内の神経免疫系に悪影響を及ぼし、認知機能低下や神経変性疾患のリスクを上昇させる可能性が示唆される。

title: Antisense transcription reveals disease-associated adaptations in the human gut microbiome.
abstract: The gut microbiome is a dynamic ecosystem in which microorganisms constantly adjust their transcriptional programmes. Here we developed metastrand, a framework that integrates strand-aware metatranscriptomics and metagenomics to quantify mRNAs and antisense RNAs (asRNAs) in complex microbial communities at gene-level resolution. In inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), microbial asRNA programmes converged across patients during active disease, correlated with faecal metabolites and calprotectin levels and remained stable during persistent inflammation, highlighting their potential as biomarkers of inflammatory activity in the gut. These programmes involved antisense-to-sense transcriptional shifts at insertion sequence elements with functionally diverse passenger genes and preceded their detection at new genomic locations, linking asRNA dynamics to structural genome rearrangements and redistribution of adaptive functions under selective pressure. Similar dynamics were observed in a mouse model of colitis, oxidative stress in vitro and in patients with pathogen-confirmed gastroenteritis, establishing asRNAs as an important dimension of microbial adaptation in health and disease.
authors: Pust MM, Mohamed AMT, Stražar M, Arias-Rojas A, Cunningham-Oakes E, Brown EM, Bumber A, Pishchany G, Li C, Ananthakrishnan AN, Darby AC, Vlamakis H, Plichta DR, Xavier RJ.
screening_reason: The paper focuses on metatranscriptomic profiling of antisense RNA dynamics and transcriptional adaptation within the human gut microbiome.
summary_ja: 本研究では、ストランド認識型メタトランスクリプトミクスとメタゲノミクスを統合し、腸内細菌叢のアンチセンスRNA（asRNA）を高解像度で定量する解析ツール「metastrand」を開発した。炎症性腸疾患（IBD）患者の活動期において細菌のasRNA発現パターンが収束し、便中カルプロテクチンなどの炎症指標と相関することが示された。asRNAの動態は挿入配列エレメントにおけるアンチセンスからセンスへの転写シフトを引き起こし、ゲノム構造の再編に先立って適応機能を提示していた。同様の現象はマウスの大腸炎モデルや病原体感染性胃腸炎患者でも確認され、asRNAが病態適応の重要な要素であることが明らかになった。
summary_en: Researchers established metastrand, an analytical platform integrating strand-aware metatranscriptomics and metagenomics to quantify bacterial mRNA and antisense RNA dynamics. In inflammatory bowel disease, gut microbial antisense RNA profiles converged during active disease and correlated with fecal inflammatory markers. These antisense RNA shifts preceded genomic rearrangements, demonstrating that antisense transcription serves as a key mechanism for microbial adaptation during inflammation.
key_finding_ja: 腸内細菌のアンチセンスRNA転写動態は、炎症性腸疾患などの病態におけるゲノム再編と環境適応を駆動する。
why_it_matters_ja: 腸内細菌の病態適応メカニズムの理解を深め、炎症性腸疾患の新たな診断バイオマーカーや治療標的の開発につながる可能性がある。

title: Biomimetic exosomal delivery of ginsenoside Rd reduces post-stroke depression via microglial reprogramming in a pathway involving EGFR/JAK2/STAT3.
abstract: Post-stroke depression (PSD) represents a complex neuropsychiatric challenge characterized by persistent neuroinflammation and synaptic dysfunction, yet effective therapeutic interventions are constrained by the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and the lack of specific targets. Using a multidimensional screening strategy for Chaihu-Jia-Longgu-Muli Decoction (CLM), we identified ginsenoside Rd (Rd) as a key blood-absorbed bioactive constituent associated with Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (EGFR) signaling. To overcome the bioavailability bottleneck, a biomimetic nanodelivery system is engineered by encapsulating Rd into microglia-derived exosomes (Exos@Rd). Based on the reported lesion-homing properties of microglia-derived exosomes, we developed a biomimetic Exos@Rd delivery system. Exosomal loading markedly enhanced the brain accumulation of Rd compared with free Rd. Mechanistically, it is demonstrated that aberrant EGFR activation functions as an upstream regulator of the JAK2/STAT3 cascade in microglia. Exos@Rd effectively suppressed this pathway and promoted anti-inflammatory microglial reprogramming, characterized by a shift from an M1-associated pro-inflammatory state toward an M2-associated anti-inflammatory profile. This microglia-centered anti-inflammatory regulation was accompanied by reduced oxidative stress and restoration of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), postsynaptic density protein 95 (PSD95) and Synapsin I (SYN1) expression. In a PSD mouse model, Exos@Rd significantly restores cerebral perfusion and alleviates depressive-like behaviors. Collectively, this study elucidates a novel EGFR-driven neuroinflammatory mechanism and presents a bio-inspired strategy for precision CNS drug delivery, offering a promising therapeutic paradigm for PSD.
authors: Chen J, Yin X, Yan D, Shi Q, Tan E, Yan Z, Zhang P, Li W, Xiao M, Wang Q, Fan Q, Li P, Liu J.
screening_reason: The study focuses on microglial anti-inflammatory reprogramming and neuroinflammation modulation in post-stroke depression.
summary_ja: 脳卒中後うつ病（PSD）は持続的な神経炎症と神経伝達の機能障害を特徴とするが、血流脳関門の存在が標的治療の障害となっている。本研究では、ミクログリア由来エクソソームにジンセノシドRdを内包させたナノ製剤（Exos@Rd）を構築し、脳内送達効率を大幅に向上させた。メカニズム解析により、ミクログリアにおけるEGFR/JAK2/STAT3経路の過剰活性化が神経炎症を誘導すること、ならびにExos@Rdが同経路を抑制してM2抗炎症型表現型への再プログラミングを促進することが示された。PSDマウスモデルにおいて、Exos@Rd投与は脳血流を改善し、シナプス関連因子の発現を回復させてうつ様行動を軽減させた。
summary_en: To address the therapeutic challenges of post-stroke depression, researchers engineered a biomimetic exosomal delivery system encapsulating ginsenoside Rd (Exos@Rd). Exos@Rd targeted microglial aberrant EGFR activation and suppressed the downstream JAK2/STAT3 signaling cascade, promoting anti-inflammatory microglial reprogramming. In a mouse model of post-stroke depression, Exos@Rd treatment restored cerebral perfusion, reduced oxidative stress, upregulated synaptic markers, and significantly attenuated depressive-like behaviors.
key_finding_ja: ミクログリア由来エクソソームで送達したジンセノシドRdは、EGFR/JAK2/STAT3経路を抑制してミクログリアを抗炎症型に再プログラミングし、脳卒中後うつ病モデルマウスの症状を改善した。
why_it_matters_ja: 脳卒中後うつ病の病態におけるEGFRシグナルの関与が明らかになり、エクソソームを利用した脳指向性ナノドラッグデリバリーの有用性が示された。

title: Systematic profiling of growth interactions in human gut microbiome species.
abstract: Microbial interactions shape the composition and stability of the human gut microbiome. Yet, few studies have systematically investigated species-species growth interactions and the mechanisms behind these. Here we show that among 36 representative gut bacterial strains, when two species interact, the interactions are mostly inhibitory. To provide biological insight into specific interactions, we further investigate the basis of a positive interaction, showing that Clostridium perfringens promotes the growth of Mediterraneibacter gnavus through extracellular vesicles. Additionally, we identify Veillonella parvula as a species capable of modulating environmental pH, thereby enabling the growth of Parabacteroides merdae, a strain highly sensitive to acidic conditions. This pH-increasing effect is enhanced by guanine supplementation and persists in multi-species communities containing different pH-lowering strains from diverse bacterial phyla. Although V. parvula is commonly present in human gut microbiomes, it is generally found at low levels. Given the spatial organization of bacteria in the gut, the local pH modulation by V. parvula might support the growth of acid-sensitive strains. Overall, the comprehensive dataset and mechanistic insights presented here provide a starting point to predict microbiome composition by integrating growth interactions.
authors: Buyanbadrakh B, Baland E, Lambeck P, Pérez Jiménez L, Holmberg SM, Puértolas-Balint F, Toh E, Wai SN, Schroeder BO, Ramstedt M, Zhu S, Mateus A.
screening_reason: Directly investigates growth interactions and metabolic modulation among human gut bacterial species.
summary_ja: ヒト腸内細菌叢の代表的な36菌株を用いて、菌株間の増殖相互作用を包括的に解析した研究である。2菌種間の相互作用の多くは抑制的であったが、一部でポジティブな相互作用とその機構が同定された。例えば、Clostridium perfringensは細胞外小胞を介してMediterraneibacter gnavusの増殖を促進することが示された。さらに、Veillonella parvulaによる環境pHの上昇が、酸に弱いParabacteroides merdaeの増殖を可能にすることが明らかにされた。
summary_en: This study systematically evaluated pairwise growth interactions among 36 representative human gut bacterial strains, finding that interspecies interactions were predominantly inhibitory. The authors delineated specific positive interactions, showing that Clostridium perfringens promotes Mediterraneibacter gnavus growth via extracellular vesicles. Additionally, Veillonella parvula was found to raise environmental pH, facilitating the growth of acid-sensitive Parabacteroides merdae.
key_finding_ja: ヒト腸内細菌36株の解析により、菌種間相互作用の多くが抑制的である一方、細胞外小胞やpH調節を介した促進的相互作用機構が解明された。
why_it_matters_ja: 腸内細菌同士の相互作用メカニズムを理解することは、複雑な腸内微生物群集の構成予測や制御手法の開発に貢献する可能性がある。

title: From Dysbiosis to systemic health: Microbiome modulation as a unified therapeutic framework.
abstract: The gut microbiome is a dynamic microbial ecosystem regulating gastrointestinal, metabolic, immune, and neurobehavioral physiology. Dysbiosis has been linked to irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), and systemic disorders including metabolic syndrome, autoimmune conditions, and neurodegenerative diseases. This narrative review synthesizes mechanistic, clinical, and translational evidence to delineate molecular pathways of microbiome-targeted interventions, evaluates clinical outcomes in IBS and IBD, and proposes a unified framework linking gastrointestinal modulation to systemic health. A structured literature search across PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar (2012-2024) identified approximately 68 eligible sources, appraised using Cochrane Risk of Bias 2.0 and AMSTAR-2. Five principal molecular pathways were identified: competitive pathogen exclusion, epithelial barrier reinforcement, immune modulation, short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) production, and neurotransmitter signaling. Clinically, dietary strategies, biological agents (probiotics, prebiotics, synbiotics, postbiotics, and fecal microbiota transplantation [FMT]), advanced modalities (rifaximin, psychobiotics, bacteriophage therapy), and lifestyle interventions collectively engage these pathways. The same mechanisms underpin emerging applications in metabolic, autoimmune, neurological, and cardiovascular disease. We propose a three-tier model progressing from molecular mechanisms through gastrointestinal outcomes to systemic benefits, with precision medicine and standardized trial designs as prerequisites for therapeutic translation.
authors: Dhiman NK, Ahmad SR.
screening_reason: The review directly focuses on the gut microbiome, intestinal microbial metabolism, and host-microbe interactions.
summary_ja: 本総説は、腸内細菌叢の乱れと全身性疾患との関連について、2012年から2024年の文献を統合して概観している。病原体の競合的排除、上皮バリア強化、免疫調節、短鎖脂肪酸産生、神経伝達物質シグナル伝達の5つの主要分子経路が整理された。食事療法や生体製剤、糞便微生物移植などが過敏性腸症候群や炎症性腸疾患のほか、全身疾患の治療に応用され得る。分子機構から消化管のアウトカム、全身への影響へと至る3段階の統一モデルが提案されている。
summary_en: This narrative review synthesizes literature on gut microbiome modulation and its connection to systemic health. It highlights five core molecular pathways, including pathogen exclusion, epithelial barrier reinforcement, immune modulation, short-chain fatty acid production, and neurotransmitter signaling. The authors propose a three-tier framework connecting molecular mechanisms to gastrointestinal outcomes and systemic benefits.
key_finding_ja: 腸内細菌叢の介入による主要な5つの分子経路が整理され、分子機序から消化管および全身の健康へと繋がる3段階の統一的フレームワークが提案された。
why_it_matters_ja: 精密医療や治験デザインの標準化が進むことで、腸内細菌叢を標的とした治療法がさまざまな全身性疾患に応用される可能性が期待される。

title: Akkermansia muciniphila gavage alleviates depression-like behaviors in female A53T α-synuclein transgenic mice.
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is characterized not only by progressive motor deficits but also by non-motor symptoms, such as depression, which often emerge during the prodromal stage and significantly impair quality of life. While Akkermansia muciniphila (AKK) has shown potential in modulating neuroinflammation, its specific role and underlying mechanisms in alleviating PD-associated non-motor symptoms remain unclear. In this study, we investigated the effects of AKK intervention in 16-month-old female A53T α-synuclein (α-syn) transgenic mice. Behavioral assessments revealed that oral administration of AKK significantly ameliorated depression-like behaviors, evidenced by reduced immobility in the forced swim test and increased sucrose preference, without affecting motor function, spatial memory, or gastrointestinal motility. Mechanistically, the intervention exhibited genotype-specific effects: AKK significantly increased plasma 5-HT levels in C57 mice. This increase was associated with an enrichment of Lactobacillus taiwanensis and metabolic pathways favoring peripheral tryptophan conversion. Conversely, in A53T mice, the treatment specifically elevated hippocampal 5-HT levels without altering plasma concentrations. This central effect correlated with distinct microbial remodeling, characterized by the enrichment of butyrate/propionate-producing Lachnospiraceae and the activation of purine degradation. Collectively, these findings provide novel mechanistic insights into the therapeutic potential of AKK for managing non-motor symptoms in PD. While limited to a female cohort, our results suggest that AKK ameliorates depression-like behaviors in PD through sex-specific remodeling of the gut microbiome and serotonergic signaling.
authors: Li S, Chu X, Deng R, Zheng W, Suo X, Sun G, Liu H, Geng M, Tian J, Zhang Y.
screening_reason: The study directly examines how gut microbiome modulation via Akkermansia muciniphila alters central neurochemistry and neuroinflammation to impact behavior.
summary_ja: 本研究は、16か月齢の雌性A53T α-シヌクレイントランスジェニックマウスを用いて、Akkermansia muciniphila（AKK）投与の効果を検証した。AKKの経口投与は、運動機能や消化管運動に影響を与えることなく、うつ様行動を有意に改善した。A53Tマウスでは、AKK投与により海馬のセロトニンレベルが特異的に上昇し、酪酸やプロピオン酸を産生するLachnospiraceaeの増加を伴う腸内細菌叢の改変が確認された。
summary_en: This study examined the effects of oral Akkermansia muciniphila (AKK) administration in 16-month-old female A53T alpha-synuclein transgenic mice modeling Parkinson's disease. AKK treatment significantly alleviated depression-like behaviors without altering motor function or gut motility. In A53T mice, AKK elevated hippocampal serotonin levels and induced gut microbiota remodeling, including the enrichment of short-chain fatty acid-producing Lachnospiraceae.
key_finding_ja: 雌性A53Tパーキンソン病モデルマウスにおいて、Akkermansia muciniphilaの経口投与が腸内細菌叢の再編成と海馬セロトニン量の上昇を伴い、うつ様行動を改善した。
why_it_matters_ja: 特定の腸内細菌投与による腸内環境と中枢神経系の調節が、パーキンソン病の非運動症状に対する新たな管理手段となる可能性が示唆される。

title: The Gut Microbiome in Foodborne Microplastic Toxicity: Mechanistic Insights and Human Health Risk Assessment.
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are emerging foodborne contaminants with increasing implications for gastrointestinal health. However, the mechanistic basis linking dietary MP exposure to gut dysbiosis and intestinal dysfunction remains poorly resolved, limiting robust human health risk assessment. This review critically synthesizes current evidence on foodborne MPs, dietary exposure, and the physicochemical determinants of gastrointestinal fate, bioavailability, and toxicity. We examine the molecular and microbiome-mediated mechanisms linking MPs exposure to intestinal dysbiosis, barrier dysfunction, oxidative stress, immune activation, and metabolic reprogramming. Particular attention is given to the role of MPs as vectors for co-contaminants, which can amplify toxicity through synergistic interactions and reshape host-microbiome responses. We highlight advances in dynamic colon simulation and integrated multi-omics that unravels the mechanism underlying MP-induced intestinal toxicity. Current evidence indicates that gut microbiome dysregulation is a key mechanism driving foodborne MP-induced intestinal dysfunction and systemic toxicity. This review integrates multidisciplinary evidence to identify critical knowledge gaps and guide future research on the mechanisms, exposure, and health risks of foodborne microplastics.
authors: Iqbal MZ, Sharma P, Shafi Z, Shahid M, Debnath A, Rasool A, Ali S.
screening_reason: Centrally reviews foodborne microplastic toxicity driven by gut microbiome dysbiosis and host-microbe interactions.
summary_ja: 本総説は、経口摂取されるマイクロプラスチック（MP）による毒性と腸内細菌叢との関連について最近の知見をまとめたものである。MPの暴露は腸内細菌叢の乱れ、上皮バリア機能障害、酸化ストレス、免疫活性化、代謝リプログラミングを引き起こすことが示されている。また、MPは複合汚染物質の担体として作用し、相乗的に毒性を増強する可能性が指摘されている。マルチオミクス解析や人工腸管シミュレーションの進展により、MP誘発性の腸管障害における微生物叢の重要性が明示されている。
summary_en: This review synthesizes current evidence on how dietary microplastics affect gastrointestinal health through microbiome-mediated mechanisms. Microplastic exposure induces gut dysbiosis, barrier dysfunction, oxidative stress, and immune activation, while also acting as a vector for co-contaminants. Dysregulation of the gut microbiome is highlighted as a primary driver of microplastic-induced intestinal and systemic toxicity.
key_finding_ja: 食品由来マイクロプラスチックの毒性発現において、腸内細菌叢の撹乱が腸管障害および全身毒性を引き起こす主要な機序であることが示された。
why_it_matters_ja: 食品中のマイクロプラスチックがヒトの健康に及ぼすリスクの評価や対策の策定において、腸内細菌叢を介したメカニズムの理解が不可欠となる。

title: Single-Nucleus Transcriptomics Identifies Microglial Interferon Regulatory Factor 5 as a Regulator of Neuroinflammation During Heart Failure Progression After Myocardial Infarction in Rats.
abstract: Background The paraventricular nucleus (PVN) of the hypothalamus is a key autonomic and cardiovascular regulatory center that contributes to neuroinflammation-driven sympathetic excitation in heart failure. To define the cellular and transcriptional mechanisms underlying inflammatory signaling during heart failure progression, we performed single-nucleus RNA sequencing of the PVN in rats 2 weeks after myocardial infarction (MI). Methods PVN tissues were collected 2 weeks post MI for single-nucleus RNA sequencing analysis. Sequencing data were processed through alignment, dimensionality reduction, clustering, and marker-gene identification to define cell populations and gene expression profiles. Gene Set Variation Analysis and transcriptional regulatory network analyses were performed to identify altered signaling pathways and key transcription factors. Results A total of 16 341 nuclei were classified into 5 major cell types: neurons, oligodendrocytes, astrocytes, oligodendrocyte progenitor cells, and microglia. Functional analyses identified microglia as the primary mediators of inflammatory responses in the PVN. Gene Set Variation Analysis revealed substantial pathway alterations across cell types, with microglia exhibiting marked activation of immune-related and cytokine-producing pathways in MI rats. Moreover, IRF5 (interferon regulatory factor 5) was identified as a master transcriptional regulator associated with inflammatory activation and was significantly upregulated in PVN microglia after MI. Increased IRF5 expression in PVN microglia was confirmed by immunofluorescence. Conclusions Single-nucleus RNA sequencing identified distinct cell-specific gene signatures, regulatory networks, and signaling pathways in the PVN during heart failure, with microglial IRF5 emerging as a central regulator of immune activation and inflammatory processes. Activated IRF5 promotes microglial activation and neuroinflammation, thereby enhancing PVN neuronal activity and driving sympathetic and neurohumoral dysregulation in rats with MI. Targeting IRF5 and its downstream pathways may therefore provide new insights into the central inflammatory mechanisms contributing to cardiac dysfunction during heart failure progression.
authors: Tang W, Yu Y, Bing JY, Tong L, Weiss RM, Wei SG.
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
screening_reason: Focuses on microglial IRF5 as a master regulator of central neuroinflammation in the hypothalamic PVN.
summary_ja: 心筋梗塞後の心不全進行における視床下部室傍核（PVN）の神経炎症メカニズムを解明するため、ラットを用いて単一核RNAシーケンス解析を実施した。PVNにおける主要な細胞群のうち、ミクログリアが炎症反応の主要な仲介者であることが同定された。転写因子IRF5が心筋梗塞後のミクログリアで顕著に発現上昇しており、免疫活性化を主導していることが見出された。ミクログリアのIRF5活性化は神経炎症を促進し、PVN神経活性の亢進を介して交感神経系の失調を引き起こす。
summary_en: Single-nucleus RNA sequencing of the hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus in post-myocardial infarction rats identified microglia as key drivers of inflammatory signaling. The transcription factor IRF5 was significantly upregulated in microglia, promoting neuroinflammation and microglial activation. This microglial IRF5 activation enhances neuronal activity in the paraventricular nucleus, contributing to sympathetic dysregulation during heart failure progression.
key_finding_ja: 心筋梗塞後の視床下部室傍核においてミクログリアのIRF5が顕著に上昇し、神経炎症と交感神経の過剰活性化を駆動する中心因子であることが明らかになった。
why_it_matters_ja: 心不全に伴う神経体液性調節異常の治療において、ミクログリアのIRF5およびその下流経路が新たな標的となる可能性が示唆される。

title: PDCD1 Signaling in Microglia Can Reduce Neuroinflammation and Apoptosis Induced by Traumatic Brain Injury by Regulating PI3K/Akt Signaling Pathway, Thereby Alleviating Neurological Dysfunction.
abstract: Following traumatic brain injury (TBI), inflammation of the nerve and death of nerve cells are intimately associated with the unfavorable prognosis of TBI patients. This study aims to examine the function of programmed cell death protein-1 (PDCD1) signaling in neuroinflammation and nerve cell death following TBI in mice, as well as its impact on the recuperation of cognitive, memory, and motor capabilities, and to initially analyze its underlying mechanism. In vivo investigations employed a controlled cortical impact (CCI) murine model. BV-2 cells were activated with lipopolysaccharide (LPS) to create an in vitro model of microglial inflammation. The outcome indicates that TBI significantly and temporarily increased the expression of PDCD1 in vivo, with PDCD1 mostly expressed in microglia and neurons, but not in astrocytes. Knockdown of PDCD1 led to an increase in the protein expression levels of IL-1β, iNOS, and Bax, whereas the levels of Bcl-2, p-PI3K, and p-Akt dropped. Nonetheless, the overexpression of PDCD1 yielded contrary outcomes; furthermore, LY294002 may partially counteract the effects of PDCD1 overexpression and diminish its expression levels. And the results of further cell experiments in vitro were consistent with those in vivo. PDCD1 expression is elevated in both in vivo TBI models and in vitro microglial inflammation models. Moreover, PDCD1 mitigates neuroinflammation and nerve cell death, at least partially, via the PI3K/Akt pathway.
authors: Tian J, Wang Y, Zhao J, Guo Z, Jiang L, Zhou L, Yin Y, Ding S, Wang L, Lu Y, Zhang Y.
screening_reason: Directly examines PDCD1 signaling in microglial neuroinflammation following traumatic brain injury.
summary_ja: 頭部外傷（TBI）マウスモデルおよびLPS刺激BV-2ミクログリア細胞を用いて、PDCD1シグナルの役割を評価した。TBI後にPDCD1発現は一過性に上昇し、主としてミクログリアおよび神経細胞に認められた。PDCD1のノックダウンは炎症性因子やプロアポトーシス因子の増加を招いた一方、過剰発現はPI3K/Akt経路を介して神経炎症と細胞死を抑制した。インビトロ実験においてもインビボと同様の結果が得られ、PDCD1の神経保護作用機序が示された。
summary_en: Using a murine traumatic brain injury model and cultured BV-2 microglial cells, this study evaluated the protective role of PDCD1 signaling. PDCD1 expression was acutely increased in microglia and neurons following injury. Overexpression of PDCD1 reduced neuroinflammation and cell death via activation of the PI3K/Akt pathway, whereas knockdown exacerbated these pathological responses.
key_finding_ja: ミクログリアにおけるPDCD1シグナルがPI3K/Akt経路を活性化することで、頭部外傷後の神経炎症と細胞死を軽減することが示された。
why_it_matters_ja: PDCD1シグナル経路を可塑的に制御することが、頭部外傷後の神経機能障害軽減に向けた治療標的となる可能性を示している。

title: Fumarate hydratase suppresses glioblastoma progression by restricting fumarate-mediated succination of TRIM17.
abstract: Emerging evidence indicates that metabolic reprogramming plays a pivotal role in glioblastoma (GBM) progression. Here, we report that the expression of fumarate hydratase (FH) is significantly reduced in GBM patient samples. FH overexpression suppresses the viability, migration, and invasion of GBM cells, whereas FH knockdown or pharmacological inhibition produces the opposite effects. Consistent with FH downregulation, its substrate fumarate accumulates in GBM cells and clinical tumor tissues. As a result, excess fumarate induces succination of TRIM17 at Cys370, thereby reducing TRIM17 protein stability and impairing its E3 ubiquitin ligase activity. Subsequent functional studies identify TRIM17 as a tumor suppressor in GBM. In vivo xenograft models further confirm that FH restrains GBM progression by regulating TRIM17 succination. Collectively, these findings establish FH as a negative regulator of GBM and reveal a fumarate-TRIM17 signaling axis that promotes GBM malignancy through post-translational modification of TRIM17.
authors: Ju Q, Hu Y, Gong C, Wu R, Shen M, Wang X, Tang X, Shen J, Sun C.
screening_reason: The study provides a mechanistic investigation of covalent protein post-translational modification via fumarate-mediated succination of TRIM17.
summary_ja: 膠芽腫（GBM）においてフマル酸ヒドラターゼ（FH）の発現低下が確認され、FHの過剰発現はGBM細胞の生存や浸潤を抑制することが示された。FH低下により基質であるフマル酸が蓄積し、TRIM17のCys370部位でサクシネーションが誘導される。これによりTRIM17のタンパク質安定性とE3ユビキチンリガーゼ活性が低下し、腫瘍抑制機能が阻害される。マウス異種移植モデルでも、FHがTRIM17のサクシネーション制御を介してGBMの進行を抑制することが確認された。
summary_en: Reduced expression of fumarate hydratase (FH) in glioblastoma leads to fumarate accumulation, which induces succination of TRIM17 at Cys370. This post-translational modification decreases TRIM17 stability and ubiquitin ligase activity, thereby impairing its tumor-suppressive functions. In vivo experiments confirm that FH suppresses glioblastoma progression through this fumarate-TRIM17 signaling axis.
key_finding_ja: フマル酸ヒドラターゼの低下によるフマル酸の蓄積がTRIM17のサクシネーションを誘導し、その腫瘍抑制機能を損なうことで膠芽腫の悪性化を促進することが解明された。
why_it_matters_ja: フマル酸によるタンパク質修飾を標的とした新たな治療アプローチが、膠芽腫の進行抑制に役立つ可能性を示唆している。

title: Tetrandrine attenuates hypoxia-induced microglial M1 polarization and microglia-mediated photoreceptor cell injury through modulation of NF-κB/p65 signaling.
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR), a primary cause of working-age vision loss, is characterized by neuroinflammation, in which microglial polarization toward the proinflammatory M1 phenotype serves as a pivotal driver. Reprogramming microglia toward an anti-inflammatory and reparative phenotype may therefore represent a promising therapeutic strategy. This study investigated the effects of tetrandrine (Tet) on hypoxia-induced microglial activation and explored the underlying mechanisms. We established a chemical hypoxia model using CoCl 2 and evaluated inflammatory mediators and associated molecules by qRT-PCR, western blotting, and immunofluorescence. Microglial migratory and phagocytic functions were assessed by scratch wound and phagocytosis assays, respectively. Potential drug targets were identified through an integrative approach combining network pharmacology, molecular docking, and cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA). Tet suppressed CoCl 2 -induced M1-associated inflammatory gene expression in BV2 cells and attenuated p65 activation and cytotoxic responses in HMC3 cells. Functionally, Tet restored impaired phagocytic capacity, attenuated aberrant migration, and mitigated microglia-mediated injury to 661W photoreceptor-derived cells. Mechanistic analyses showed that Tet reduced p65 phosphorylation and apparent nuclear accumulation, thereby limiting activation of the HIF-1α/NF-κB signaling axis; docking and CETSA findings further supported a potential interaction between Tet and p65. In summary, Tet alleviates hypoxia-induced microglial M1 polarization and microglia-mediated photoreceptor cell injury, at least partly through modulation of NF-κB/p65 signaling. These findings identify Tet as a candidate compound for further preclinical investigation in retinal neuroinflammation associated with DR.
authors: Wang S, Zhang G, Xu C, Jia Z, Lu H.
screening_reason: Investigates the attenuation of microglial M1 polarization and retinal neuroinflammation by tetrandrine.
summary_ja: 本研究では、低酸素誘導性のミクログリア活性化および光受容体細胞傷害に対するテトランドリン（Tet）の効果とその分子機構を検証した。CoCl2処理による低酸素モデル細胞において、TetはBV2細胞のM1型炎症性遺伝子発現を抑制し、HMC3細胞におけるp65の活性化を減弱させた。さらにTetは低下した貪食能を回復させ、異常な細胞遊走を抑え、661W光受容体由来細胞の傷害を軽減した。メカニズム解析により、Tetはp65のリン酸化と核内集積を抑制し、HIF-1α/NF-κBシグナル軸の活性化を抑えることが示された。
summary_en: This study investigated the therapeutic potential of tetrandrine against hypoxia-induced microglial activation and photoreceptor cell injury. In cellular hypoxia models, tetrandrine suppressed microglial M1 polarization, restored phagocytic capacity, and protected 661W photoreceptor-derived cells from cytotoxic injury. Mechanistically, tetrandrine inhibited p65 phosphorylation and nuclear accumulation, thereby modulating the HIF-1α/NF-κB signaling axis.
key_finding_ja: テトランドリンはNF-κB/p65シグナル伝達を調節することで、低酸素誘導性のミクログリアM1分極および光受容体細胞傷害を抑える。
why_it_matters_ja: 糖尿病網膜症に伴う網膜神経炎症を標的とした新たな治療薬候補として前臨床研究の進展が期待される。

title: Four Decades of Stress, Depression, and Close Relationships: Lessons from Psychoneuroimmunology.
abstract: Human psychoneuroimmunology research has demonstrated that stress, depression, and close relationships reliably shape immune and endocrine function in ways that matter for health. Across studies of examination stress, laboratory stressors, marital discord, cancer survivorship, and dementia caregiving, psychosocial adversity predicts more infections, weaker vaccine responses and faster erosion of vaccine protection, slower wound healing, heightened inflammation, and accelerated cellular aging. Depression also sensitizes immune function, producing larger inflammatory responses when individuals encounter stressors. Loneliness, low support, and distressed relationships can amplify stress reactivity and are linked to greater inflammatory and metabolic vulnerability, including postprandial inflammatory and endothelial responses. More recent work has extended these pathways to the gut microbiome and intestinal permeability (leaky gut), integrating microbial, neuroendocrine, and immune mechanisms. Collectively, the evidence supports a biobehavioral model in which social stress accelerates immune aging and increases risk for inflammation-related disease, while behavioral and nutritional interventions can modify these trajectories.
authors: Kiecolt-Glaser JK.
screening_reason: The review focuses centrally on psychoneuroimmunology, neuroendocrine-immune interactions, and their integration with gut microbiome mechanisms.
summary_ja: 本レビューは、心理社会的ストレス、うつ病、対人関係が免疫機能および内分泌機能に与える影響について、40年間にわたる精神神経免疫学の研究をまとめている。心理的逆境は炎症の増強、ワクチン応答の低下、創傷治癒の遅延、細胞老化の加速を引き起こす。さらに、近年の研究ではこれらの経路に腸内細菌叢や腸管透過性（リーキーガット）が組み込まれ、行動的・栄養的介入の可能性が提示されている。
summary_en: This review synthesizes four decades of psychoneuroimmunology research on how stress, depression, and social relationships affect immune and endocrine functioning. Psychosocial adversity and depression promote systemic inflammation, impair vaccine responses, and accelerate immune aging. Recent advances incorporate the gut microbiome and intestinal permeability into biobehavioral models that guide potential behavioral and nutritional interventions.
key_finding_ja: 心理社会的ストレスとうつ病が神経内分泌・免疫経路および腸内細菌叢や腸管透過性を介して全身性炎症や免疫老化を促進することが示された。
why_it_matters_ja: 精神神経免疫学的なメカニズムの解明により、ストレス関連疾患や免疫機能障害に対する行動・栄養介入の有用性が示唆される。

title: Molecular mechanisms of nicotinic acetylcholine receptors in mood dysregulation.
abstract: Mood disorders are complex neurobiological disorders in which cholinergic signaling plays a key role in modulating affective states. Nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (nAChRs) of the α4β2 and α7 subtypes modulate neurotransmitter action in circuits associated with mood, synaptic plasticity, and neuroimmune interactions, particularly through microglial and astrocytic pathways. Here, we present an integrative review that accounts for the structural diversity, distribution, and functional roles of nAChRs within the central nervous system (CNS), with particular emphasis on their modulatory effects on monoaminergic, glutamatergic, and GABAergic pathways. We discuss the molecular mechanisms through which nAChRs modulate mood, including calcium-dependent signaling cascades, control of neuroinflammation, modulation of oxidative stress, and epigenetic regulation of receptor expression. Both preclinical and clinical studies have shown that nAChRs play a dual role in mood regulation and demonstrate their potential as pharmacological targets for depression and anxiety. Additionally, we discuss the translational issues and opportunities of subtype-selective ligands, epigenetic interventions, and biomarker-guided treatment approaches. Neuroimaging of nAChRs coupled with precise pharmacology could provide new options for treating psychiatric illnesses.
authors: Murthy MK, Samal D.
screening_reason: Focuses on nicotinic acetylcholine receptors in neuroimmune interactions, microglial pathways, and neuroinflammation in mood disorders.
summary_ja: 本総説は気分障害におけるニコチン性アセチルコリン受容体（nAChR）の役割と分子メカニズムを概観したものである。特にα4β2およびα7サブタイプのnAChRは、モノアミン系やグルタミン酸系などの神経伝達系とともに、ミクログリアやアストロサイトを介した神経免疫相互作用を調節している。本論文ではカルシウム依存性シグナル、神経炎症の制御、酸化ストレスの抑制、受容体発現のエピジェネティック規制などの機構を考察している。さらに、サブタイプ選択的リガンドやバイオマーカーを活用した精神疾患の創薬・トランスレーショナル研究の可能性について論じている。
summary_en: This review highlights the critical modulatory functions of nicotinic acetylcholine receptors, particularly α4β2 and α7 subtypes, in mood regulation and neuroimmune signaling. The receptors influence mood through calcium signaling cascades, neuroinflammation control, oxidative stress reduction, and epigenetic regulation across neural circuits. Subtype-selective targeting and biomarker-guided approaches present promising avenues for psychiatric drug discovery.
key_finding_ja: ニコチン性アセチルコリン受容体は神経回路と神経免疫系の双方を調節し、気分障害の重要な治療標的となる。
why_it_matters_ja: サブタイプ選択的リガンドやバイオマーカーを用いたうつ病や不安症の新規治療法開発に繋がる可能性がある。

title: Neuroprotection and Enhanced Hemoglobin Excretion by Intrathecal Clazosentan in Mice With Subarachnoid Hemorrhage.
abstract: Background Intravenous administration of clazosentan, a selective endothelin receptor subtype A antagonist, has been used as an anti-vasospastic agent. This study aimed to investigate whether intrathecal administration of clazosentan prevents neuroinflammation and affects lymphatic clearance of hemoglobin in a mouse model of acute subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH). Methods Male C57BL/6 mice (n=109) underwent prechiasmatic cisternal injection models of SAH or sham models. From 30 minutes post-modeling, mice randomly received a continuous intracerebroventricular infusion of saline or clazosentan (1, 0.2, and 0.04 μg in 192 μL of saline; defined as 50%, 10%, and 2% of the clinically achievable blood concentration, respectively) at a rate of 8 μL/h for 24 hours. The intervention effects were assessed by neurobehavioral testing, SAH grading, and immunohistochemical staining at 24 and 48 hours, and Western blotting at 24 hours post-modeling. Results Clazosentan treatment did not influence SAH grading but showed a dose-dependent trend toward improved survival in SAH mice. A comparison of saline treatment and 50% clazosentan treatment revealed that clazosentan significantly suppressed post-SAH neurological deterioration, hemoglobin infiltration into the brain, and induction of ionized calcium-binding adapter molecule 1 and tenascin-C in the brain, and significantly upregulated vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-3 in the brain without affecting vascular endothelial growth factor-C levels. When comparing the effects of different clazosentan doses, an inhibitory effect on neuroinflammation was observed up to 10% clazosentan. At 48 hours post-modeling, clazosentan administration dose-dependently inhibited neurological deterioration, hemoglobin infiltration into the brain and activation of perivascular macrophages and microglia, and increased hemoglobin deposition in the deep cervical lymph nodes of SAH mice without intracranial lymphatic vessel proliferation. Conclusions This study first showed that intrathecal administration of clazosentan can suppress early brain injury in terms of neuroinflammation at cerebrospinal fluid concentrations one-tenth of the clinically achievable blood concentrations, associated with enhanced lymphatic drainage of hemoglobin.
authors: Kawakita F, Hakozaki K, Aoki K, Suzuki H.
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
screening_reason: Investigates the suppressive effects of intrathecal clazosentan on neuroinflammation and microglial activation after subarachnoid hemorrhage.
summary_ja: 急性くも膜下出血（SAH）マウスモデルを用い、エンドセリンA受容体拮抗薬クラゾセンタンの髄腔内投与が神経炎症とヘモグロビン排出に与える影響を検証した。臨床血中濃度の10分の1に相当する用量の脳室内持続投与により、後遺症としての神経機能悪化、脳内ヘモグロビン浸潤、Iba1およびテナシンCの発現増加が有意に抑制された。さらに、髄腔内投与は頭蓋内リンパ管増殖を伴わずに深頸リンパ節へのヘモグロビン堆積を促進し、VEGFR-3の発現を上昇させた。48時間後においても血管周囲マクロファージやミクログリアの活性化抑制効果が維持されていた。
summary_en: Continuous intrathecal administration of clazosentan was evaluated in a mouse model of acute subarachnoid hemorrhage. Intrathecal delivery at lower doses significantly reduced neuroinflammation, microglial activation, and post-SAH neurological deterioration. Additionally, clazosentan enhanced hemoglobin excretion into deep cervical lymph nodes via upregulated VEGFR-3 signaling.
key_finding_ja: クラゾセンタンの髄腔内投与は低用量で神経炎症を抑え、リンパ系を介したヘモグロビン排出を促進する。
why_it_matters_ja: くも膜下出血後の早期脳損傷に対する髄腔内局所投与という新たな治療アプローチの可能性が示唆される。

title: Baicalin-loaded MOF-818 nanozyme for ischemic stroke treatment via ROS scavenging and neuroinflammation suppression.
abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) reperfusion induces neuronal damage through excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) and neuroinflammation. Baicalin (Bai) shows antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects but suffers from poor solubility and bioavailability. Metal-organic framework (MOF)-818, a zirconium-based framework with superoxide dismutase- and catalase-mimicking activity, efficiently scavenges ROS but lacks pharmacological versatility. Combining Bai with MOF-818 may offer multitarget neuroprotection in IS. To investigate the therapeutic efficacy and mechanisms of Bai-loaded MOF-818 (Bai@MOF-818) in IS. In vitro oxygen-glucose deprivation/reperfusion models using PC-12 cells and BV-2 microglia were employed to assess ROS scavenging, mitochondrial protection, apoptosis, and microglial polarization. In vivo , Bai@MOF-818 was stereotactically delivered into the ischemic core of rats subjected to transient middle cerebral artery occlusion. Neurological function, infarct volume, oxidative stress, apoptosis, and microglial polarization were evaluated. Bai@MOF-818 markedly scavenged ROS, restored mitochondrial membrane potential, and promoted M1-to-M2 microglial polarization via NF- κ B inhibition and PPAR γ activation. This led to reduced TNF- α /IL-6 and increased IL-10/Arg-1, alleviating neuroinflammation. Furthermore, Bai@MOF-818 inhibited neuronal apoptosis by suppressing Bax and cleaved caspase-3 while elevating the Bcl-2/Bax ratio. Histological analyses revealed preserved tissue integrity, enhanced neuronal survival, reduced infarct size and edema, and improved motor and sensory recovery. Bai@MOF-818 exerts synergistic antioxidant and anti-inflammatory actions, attenuates neuronal apoptosis, and enhances neurological recovery, representing a promising multitarget therapeutic for cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury.
authors: Shen W, Wang Y, Zhu X, Chen X, Wang X, Che F.
screening_reason: The study directly investigates targeted suppression of microglial neuroinflammation and microglial polarization in ischemic stroke.
summary_ja: 脳梗塞後の再灌流障害では過剰な活性酸素種（ROS）と神経炎症が細胞死を引き起こす。本研究では、抗酸化酵素様活性を持つ有機金属構造体MOF-818にバイカリンを担持したナノ酵素（Bai@MOF-818）の治療効果を検証した。細胞モデルおよびラット脳梗塞モデルにおいて、Bai@MOF-818は効率的なROS消去とミトコンドリア保護作用を示した。さらにNF-κB抑制とPPARγ活性化を介してミクログリアをM2表現型へ誘導し、神経炎症とアポトーシスを抑制した。これにより、梗塞サイズおよび脳浮腫が減少し、運動・感覚機能の回復が認められた。
summary_en: This study developed a novel nanozyme, Bai@MOF-818, combining baicalin with a metal-organic framework to target oxidative stress and neuroinflammation in ischemic stroke. In vitro and rat ischemia-reperfusion models demonstrated that Bai@MOF-818 effectively scavenged reactive oxygen species, restored mitochondrial function, and promoted microglial polarization toward an anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype via NF-κB inhibition and PPARγ activation. Consequently, the nanomedicine attenuated neuronal apoptosis, reduced infarct volume, and facilitated neurological recovery.
key_finding_ja: Bai@MOF-818ナノ酵素は、ROS消去とミクログリアのM2型への分化誘導を介して神経炎症とアポトーシスを抑え、脳梗塞モデルラットの神経機能を改善させた。
why_it_matters_ja: 活性酸素消去と神経炎症抑制を同時に標的とするナノ製剤は、脳虚血再灌流障害に対する多標的治療アプローチとして期待される。
